body: This makes it so that we skip `get_theme` if there's a `from_control` but it doesn't have a valid theme, is this intended?

this code went through a couple iterations until I got it to fully work. the `get_theme()` is part of a previous iteration and it worked but only if the theme was assigned to the current node.
(I just did some tests and compared with 4.4 behaviour, variations are not available to a node with theme assigned in 4.4)

`from_control` is obtained through `get_theme_owner_node()`, and it's very difficult to follow what exactly happens inside that function, the code is a bit spaghetty.
but I call `is_valid()` because that's what was being done by the `get_project_theme()` part.

I honestly have no idea what an invalid theme looks like and have no way of testing it, but if the node that is returned by `get_theme_owner_node()` fails to cast to `Control`, it will continue with the next condition, and the rest would be up to the `get_theme_owner_node()` method, which I would expect to return a valid `Control` with a theme or `nullptr`.
but more testing would be required.

variations are available when a control with theme is root of scene, and also when the root doesn't have a theme but a child does, and on controls with a theme. and I can't think of any other situation.
what I haven't tested is I think multiple controls with their own themes.
here the button named Control has a theme:
![Captura desde 2025-03-11 07-56-46](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5154ece2-73bd-4bb8-b221-4e6535d1d9c9)
The point is that if `from_control != nullptr && from_control.get_theme().is_null()` means no variations are fetched
Why it handles only Control and not Window?
"Invalid Theme" is just null. A Control with theme owner can still have its own Theme, so you should combine the variation lists from both.

> A Control with theme owner can still have its own Theme, so you should combine the variation lists from both.

I was aware of that situation, and learned what an invalid theme was after following the code.
I didn't take parent nodes with theme into account because I had not tested it.
I can confirm only the owned theme or direct parent theme is taken into account. It's a situation that doesn't feel very real, but could maybe happen, so I will look into it.

edit: made some changes but there is no difference. get_theme() and get_theme_owner_node() do not work at the same time. if the Control has a theme, that theme's variations are displayed, and if it doesn't, the parent's theme variations are displayed.
themes can also not be combined, only one theme works at a time. so if a node has a theme with a button variation, and the child has a theme with label variation, the child of this node will only get the label variation.

I feel like it would take an overhaul of the `theme_owner` system to get this to work, or some recursive loop to look at parent nodes for themes.

> Changing Control's theme should update property list, because the variations require re-selecting the node to appear.

it doesn't feel like that big of a deal, and it's a problem that happens with other nodes too. how would we go about doing that?

> your solution, while it's not complete, is better than the current state.

well something incomplete is always better than nothing



> Why it handles only Control and not Window?

I didn't think of a window as something that could hold a theme, I will change it.

edit: theme_type_variations can now be selected from a window with theme

What I mean is that `get_type_variation_list()` takes a list pointer, so you can call the method for multiple Theme resources with the same list, to get a combined list of available variations.

> themes can also not be combined, only one theme works at a time. so if a node has a theme with a button variation, and the child has a theme with label variation, the child of this node will only get the label variation.

You can use both variations. They might not show on the list, but they are accessible if you input the name manually.

> What I mean is that get_type_variation_list() takes a list pointer, so you can call the method for multiple Theme resources with the same list, to get a combined list of available variations.

I don't follow. are you referring to ```names```?
if so, I'm already doing that.

```get_type_variation_list()``` takes a string, fills a reference and returns void.

I think the problem is with the code I quoted:

> ```// Has a theme, so we don't want to change the theme owner,```

if a node has a valid theme it does not get assigned a `theme_owner`.
so a recursive loop would be needed to go up the tree, find all nodes with theme and add the variations, but it feels very hacky to do that.

Ok, I made the loop and it is now possible to combine themes.
![Captura desde 2025-03-18 20-57-41](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/981169e0-576f-4a54-9408-ea6ec3b65e32)

I still feel like the situations where this would be needed do not outweigh the potential performance drop that could happen with too many nodes.
So I think an editor option should be added later on to switch between the two modes if there are any performance problems.

the code might need some polishing, but I tested it and it works.

> if a node has a valid theme it does not get assigned a theme_owner.

Ah, I missed that. I tested a project theme + assigned theme. They weren't getting combined.

Still, all this loop does is traverse up node tree and it can only become slow if all of the Controls/Windows have their Theme assigned (which is not something you should do 🤔). I tested a complex GUI scene and it doesn't cause visible slowdowns. Maybe it's fine like that. Or you could reduce the number of iterations by using theme owner if node has one, instead of going to parent.
